n: Forced Labour in Supply Chains and Employment
ds: Labour obtained through coercion, deception, debt bondage, wage withholding, document retention or threats. Businesses and financial institutions encounter risks via labour intermediaries, suppliers in high-risk sectors and unusual wage patterns. Controls combine supply-chain due diligence with worker-centred escalation.

src.t: ILO, Profits and Poverty: The Economics of Forced Labour (2014)
OECD, Due Diligence Guidance for Responsible Business Conduct (2018)
FATF and APG, Financial Flows from Human Trafficking (2018)

cn.rt: Worker accounts and cards controlled by employers or recruiters, wage skimming, recruitment-fee debt and coerced loans.

rat: Worker accounts controlled by employers, cash payroll, recruitment fees and remittance to a few beneficiaries; labour providers and high-risk suppliers.

ind.cx: Payments from workers to recruiters or employers for placement, visas or training, creating debt.
ind.fp: Fees may be legitimately borne by employers in compliant models.
ind.ds: Payments from workers to recruiters or employers for placement, visas or training, creating debt.

ind.n: Wages paid to accounts controlled by employer or agent
ind.cx: Workers' pay lands in accounts accessed by employer, with cards held by employer or agent.
ind.fp: Some employers manage accounts for migrant workers with consent.
ind.ds: Signs that a third party holds the card, PIN, credentials or device, or that funds and activity belong to someone other than the named holder.
ind.cn: Account controlled or used by someone other than the holder

ind.n: Unusually low wages, deductions or accommodation charges
ind.cx: Pay after deductions is far below minimum wage standards; heavy deductions for housing, food and transport.
ind.fp: Statutory deductions and employer housing are lawful.
ind.ds: Pay after deductions is far below minimum wage standards; heavy deductions for housing, food and transport.

ind.n: Suppliers in sectors or regions with high forced-labour risk
ind.cx: Sourcing from sectors such as agriculture, fishing, garments or mining in regions flagged by credible reports.
ind.fp: Most suppliers in these areas comply.
ind.ds: Sourcing from sectors such as agriculture, fishing, garments or mining in regions flagged by credible reports.

ind.n: Labour provider with no registration or opaque ownership
ind.cx: Unlicensed gangmaster supplying workers, with nominee owners and frequent name changes.
ind.ds: Unlicensed gangmaster supplying workers, with nominee owners and frequent name changes.

ind.n: Document retention or restricted movement reported
ind.cx: Audit or customer information indicates passports withheld, workers housed on site or unable to leave.
ind.fp: Employers may safeguard documents at workers' request in limited cases.
ind.ds: Audit or customer information indicates passports withheld, workers housed on site or unable to leave.

ind.n: Adverse media or import bans related to supplier
ind.cx: Credible allegations or customs detentions connected with forced labour.
ind.ds: Counterparties, suppliers, respondents or controllers appear in adverse media, law-enforcement notices or intelligence connected to financial crime, abuse, forced labour or organised crime.
ind.cn: Adverse media or intelligence linking counterparties to criminal activity

ind.n: Payment of workers in cash with no payroll records
ind.cx: Large cash payroll withdrawals with no tax or social contributions.
ind.fp: Informal economy may lawfully include cash wages.
ind.ds: Large cash payroll withdrawals with no tax or social contributions.

ind.n: Seasonal worker mass remittance to few beneficiaries
ind.cx: Many workers all send funds to one recipient in home country.
ind.fp: Workers from one village may send to a single trusted agent.
ind.ds: Many workers all send funds to one recipient in home country.

ctl.n: Labour provider and recruiter due diligence
ctl.ds: Verifies licences, ownership, registration, tax compliance and wage-payment evidence of labour providers and recruiters at onboarding and review, and checks recruitment practices. It reduces exposure to exploitative labour supply and undeclared work.

ctl.n: Payroll and worker payment flow analytics
ctl.ds: Compares payroll flows with declared headcount, checks that wages reach workers' own accounts and flags cash payroll, recruiter payments and many-to-one wage patterns. It surfaces undeclared work and labour exploitation.

Provides protected, confidential channels for staff, workers and suppliers to report misconduct or concerns, together with conduct monitoring to surface insider collusion. It brings internal and supply-chain issues to light.

Writes compliance obligations into contracts, including representations, audit rights, termination rights for breach and minimum standards such as wage or disclosure terms. It gives the institution an enforceable lever over counterparties.

Audits suppliers and processors, including interviews and records, and requires corrective action plans and remediation with support for affected workers. It verifies conditions on the ground and drives fixes rather than only detecting problems.

Maps suppliers and sub-suppliers back through the chain, down to plot, mine or farm level where relevant, and requires traceability of key inputs to origin. It makes hidden high-risk sources visible so they can be excluded or audited.

Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.

ctl.n: Account restriction, decline and exit policy
ctl.ds: Defines when a relationship or supplier must be declined, restricted or terminated, for example for unresolved due diligence, non-cooperation or unmanageable risk, with timelines and approvers. It prevents indefinite continuation of relationships that cannot be controlled.

Runs continuous screening of customers, owners, introducers, suppliers and counterparties against curated news, leaks, regulatory notices and enforcement releases, with reliability grading and identity disambiguation. It surfaces negative information that registers and lists do not carry.

Teaches analysts to weigh several weak signals together, understand network and settlement structures, and avoid profiling on protected characteristics. It raises investigative quality and reduces both missed risk and unfair outcomes.

ctl.n: Fan-in, fan-out and funnel account detection
ctl.ds: Detects accounts receiving from many unrelated senders, or sending to many beneficiaries, followed by consolidation or onward movement. It surfaces collector, funnel and mule structures.
